stem: A six month old boy presents with right esotropia that his parents have noted for most of his life. What advice would you give his parents?

options.text: Conservative management as he is likely to grow out of the problem
He needs to be referred to an ophthalmologist as soon as possible
He needs to be referred to an ophthalmologist at the age of 2½ years
He needs to be referred to an ophthalmologist once he is old enough to cooperate for an accurate visual assessment

explanation: Persistent esotropia in an infant is not normal and should be assessed promptly by ophthalmology to evaluate for amblyopia, refractive error, or other ocular pathology. Early referral is important because delayed treatment can lead to permanent visual loss.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect. Infantile esotropia should not be managed expectantly because it may be associated with amblyopia and requires assessment.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. A 6-month-old with persistent esotropia needs prompt ophthalmology referral.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. Waiting until 2.5 years would delay evaluation and treatment of a potentially vision-threatening condition.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Referral should not wait until the child can cooperate with formal visual testing.
